prompt_en: A complex photographic scene centers on a portrait subject guided by the supplied face-and-hair reference, with a visible action unfolding at a cartographic archive light table. The newly authored subject is a 29-year-old adult woman, a map researcher, whose dark short bob, fine separated fringe, soft facial contours, deep brown eyes and natural lip shape follow the reference. She stands on the far side of the table, leaning forward comfortably in a softly draped charcoal cotton shirt with sleeves rolled below the elbows. On the same charcoal cotton shirt, its fine weave stays visible as small folds radiate from the bent elbows toward the rolled cuffs, following her forward reach while the front placket and loose silhouette stay continuous. Her left palm steadies the lower edge of a worn cream coastal map; her right thumb and index finger pinch the near corner of a transparent tracing sheet spread across it. The printed coastline and the darker traced coastline coincide through the center, then separate into two clearly visible lines near a small inlet. Her gaze follows that particular mismatch, chin slightly lowered, lips resting softly apart, curiosity carried by sustained attention rather than a performance for the camera. The lit tabletop gives the thin paper a gentle glow and picks out the fingertips, while blue dusk at a tall window outlines her hair. Shallow map drawers and a single rolled chart remain quieter behind her. Seen diagonally across the table in a medium portrait at chest height, her face, both hands and the mismatched inlet share clear focus. The foreground sheet edge leads toward the place she examines; fine paper fibers, softly creased cotton and smooth transparent film remain distinct. Natural photographic color and restrained contrast hold a quiet, intimate atmosphere around the act of comparison.
